rubrics.criterion: The link-check pipeline struct (lychee-lib/src/client.rs, struct Client) no longer re-implements the exclusion/inclusion decision chain. Excluded-or-not decisions for normal checking are made by the exclusion-policy configuration owner (lychee-lib/src/filter, struct Filter) or a cohesive component it delegates to, and no copy of the per-category decision chain (scheme rules, host/localhost rule, the loopback/private/link-local IP classifications, mail rule, reserved example domains, unsupported domains, false-positive patterns, and the include-over-exclude regular-expression precedence) remains inside the pipeline struct.
rubrics.rationale: This is the largest responsibility the pipeline absorbed: a second copy of the configured exclusion policy, read field-by-field off the filter configuration. The criterion pins the concrete policy this case duplicates, so a repair that merely hid the duplicate or left any category behind does not pass.

rubrics.criterion: Remap rule evaluation is owned again by the remap configuration component (lychee-lib/src/remap, struct Remaps): rule matching, substitution, result construction, and the evaluation order live behind that owner, and the pipeline requests evaluation instead of walking the rule list itself. The pipeline struct and other crate members no longer read the rule storage directly (the field is no longer exposed for outside-the-owner access, unless an equivalent behavior-preserving interface within the remap owner provides it).
rubrics.rationale: The injection inlined the remap table's evaluator into the pipeline and widened the table's rule-list visibility to make that possible. This criterion requires the responsibility and the encapsulation to go back together; a repair that keeps the pipeline reading the table's internals fails it.

rubrics.criterion: A dedicated per-protocol mail checking component exists again in the checker family (lychee-lib/src/checker/): it owns the mail verification engine object, its construction from the configured timeout, the address extraction plus verification-result-to-status mapping, and the feature handling for the mail dispatch. The pipeline struct neither stores the verification engine nor implements the verification procedure; it only dispatches mail URIs to the component.
rubrics.rationale: This responsibility was absorbed by deleting its component outright (lychee-lib/src/checker/mail.rs was removed together with its module registration). A repair succeeds here only by rebuilding a cohesive owner — not by keeping the engine and procedure on the pipeline or by inlining them elsewhere in the pipeline's file.

rubrics.criterion: The pipeline struct (lychee-lib/src/client.rs, struct Client) no longer carries the absorbed responsibilities' state or helper surface: its fields are its own coordination state and the delegating collaborators, and the private helpers that served only the absorbed responsibilities — including probes relaying whether the remap rule table is empty and presence/accessor helpers for the mail verification engine — are gone or moved with the responsibility they serve.
rubrics.rationale: The god-class contribution is not just duplicated code but the pipeline gaining state islands and relay methods for each absorbed job. This criterion measures the struct itself rather than any particular file list, and accepts any behavior-preserving ownership arrangement that leaves the pipeline free of them.

rubrics.criterion: The restoration is wired coherently on both ends: the restored mail checking component is reachable through the checker family the way the other per-protocol components are (its module is present in the family's module list), and the pipeline construction path (the builder entry that assembles the client in lychee-lib/src/client.rs) wires the exclusion-policy owner, the remap owner, and the mail component together consistently in both feature states.
rubrics.rationale: Deleting the mail component broke two wiring points outside the pipeline body (module registration and construction). A repair that rebuilds the owner but leaves either wiring point inconsistent — unregistered module content, or a builder wiring only one feature state — is incomplete for this case's takeover.

rubrics.criterion: The request-dispatch flow through the pipeline (the check entry point in lychee-lib/src/client.rs, including the early no-remap-rules fast path and the in-place rewriting of the checked URI before dispatch) is updated to consult the re-owned owners, with externally observable outcomes unchanged for: requests with and without remap rules, remapped-versus-unremapped logging behavior, and excluded-versus-checked requests.
rubrics.rationale: The injection restructured these call sites to talk to the absorbed inline logic (the fast-path probe and in-place rewrite). This criterion forces the call sites to be re-coupled to the re-owned components rather than being left pointing at the takeover's scaffolding, while keeping the observable dispatch outcomes fixed.

rubrics.criterion: The feature split survives the restoration in the library's established shape: with the email-check feature enabled the mail dispatch goes through the real verification owner, and without it a distinct code path with the same public signature returns excluded for mail URIs (for example the signature-matching stub convention the checker components use under the disabled feature).
rubrics.rationale: The takeover replaced the previous owner's feature-split module with a feature-split span of pipeline methods. This records that an acceptable repair must reproduce the feature-boundary behavior in the restored owner — any equivalent arrangement (e.g. keeping the stub on the dispatch entry) also passes, as long as both feature states compile and behave as before.

rubrics.criterion: The pipeline's leftover takeover artifacts are fully removed: no dead or orphaned per-category policy helpers remain in lychee-lib/src/client.rs, and no imports of the filter module's policy helper functions (false-positive, example-domain, unsupported-domain checks) stay behind in the pipeline file once the chain deletion is complete.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed exclusion chain came with helper imports and nine per-category methods. A repair that deletes the delegation but leaves methods or imports behind would keep the takeover's residue in the file, which is exactly what this case asks to be cleaned up.

rubrics.criterion: No method or field remains whose only purpose was the takeover's internal plumbing: probe and accessor helpers for the remap rule table or the mail verification engine do not survive unused on the pipeline struct, and the remap rule storage is not left readable at the wider visibility the takeover introduced (crate-readable for outside-the-owner access) after evaluation returns to the remap owner.
rubrics.rationale: The injection widened a private field's visibility and added relay helpers to make the absorbed implementations work in their new address. Leaving either in place after re-homing means the scaffolding — not just the responsibility — survived, which fails the cleanup this task asks for.

rubrics.criterion: The checker family's module list (lychee-lib/src/checker/mod.rs) is left with no registration mismatch: every registered per-protocol component exists, and every existing per-protocol component is registered, with no leftover references anywhere in the crate to positions the takeover emptied.
rubrics.rationale: The takeover removed one module registration to keep the deleted component from compiling. This criterion grades that the module list matches reality after the restoration instead of carrying the takeover's traces or a new mismatch.

rubrics.criterion: With default features enabled (email-check on), mail verification still really happens through the verification engine: a mailto URI still produces the same status mapping as before the change (a reachable address maps to a success status, an uncertain one to the unknown-mail status, an unreachable one to the unreachable-address error) rather than silently becoming excluded, or panicking on a missing engine.
rubrics.rationale: The most plausible silent failure of this repair is losing the engine hand-off: storing it on the wrong side of a feature boundary, or turning the enabled path into the excluded stub, would make mail checks quietly stop checking. This regression is barely visible in the general flow and not covered by network-free assertions.

rubrics.criterion: Remap behavior is identical to before the change: the first matching rule in evaluation order still wins, only the matched URI is rewritten and still in place before dispatch, and a rule whose replacement is not a valid URL still fails with the same invalid-remap error kind and message wording that the repository had before the takeover.
rubrics.rationale: Moving rule evaluation back across a module boundary risks re-ordering rules, dropping the in-place rewrite, or re-wording the failure message. All three change observable behavior for configured remaps, so the criterion names the exact semantics at stake.

rubrics.criterion: Exclusion behavior is identical to before the takeover for every input class of the policy: scheme rules, host exclusions with localhost treated like a loopback IP, the loopback/private/link-local IP classifications, mail handling under its include flag, tel URIs, reserved example domains, known unsupported domains, well-known false-positive patterns, and includes taking precedence over excludes.
rubrics.rationale: Removing the duplicate chain reroutes every excluded-vs-checked decision through the policy owner. The visible risk of this refactor step is a precedence or predicate slip that flips a class of links between checked and excluded, which the existing suite only pins from the owner's side.

rubrics.criterion: The library's externally visible surface is unchanged: no public type, method signature, or constructor parameter of the pipeline and its builder is added, renamed, or re-shaped by the cleanup (new owner types stay inside the crate's own organization, e.g. crate-visible), and behavior-visible status values are identical.
rubrics.rationale: Both task prompts fix this boundary explicitly to keep the repair a pure re-ownership. A repair that exposes the restored components as new public API changes the library's compatibility surface and exceeds the task's scope.
